answer: A practical defence is to make identity expensive to duplicate: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must lock a stake and build a verifiable work history. Like a grove that grows only through tended growth, reputation should accrue gradually from attested tasks, not from new accounts. Each verified action is a vine linking past work to present claims, so a fake identity cannot borrow another history. Tending a garden takes time and stake; sybils are filtered because faking that record costs real money and time, while one operator running a thousand empty identities gains nothing.
